title: Two Tickets
statement: You are given an array of ticket prices and a budget. Return the indices [i, j] (i < j) of the two tickets whose prices add up exactly to the budget. Exactly one valid pair exists, and you may not use the same ticket twice.

answerKey.pattern: One pass with a hash map from price to index (complement lookup)
keyPoints: For each index i compute need = budget - prices[i]
If need is already in the map, return [map[need], i]
Checking before inserting prevents using the same ticket twice
edgeCases: Two equal prices, e.g. [3, 3] with budget 6
Must not pair a ticket with itself
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Nested loops over all pairs: O(n^2)
Sort with original indices kept, then two pointers: O(n log n)

hints: For each price, which other price would complete the budget?
Store each price you pass in a map from price to its index.
Look for the needed price before storing the current one, so a ticket is never paired with itself.
